issues.legal_issue: A claimant may be allowed to seek a reference for compensation fixed by a supplementary award when the award was made in the claimant’s absence, the claimant timely challenged its adequacy, and the supplementary award did not record a waiver of further claims.
material_facts: The original negotiated award concerned the land and expressly barred a request to enhance the land’s market value.
The supplementary award separately fixed compensation for structures and trees based on expert valuation reports, was made in the claimant’s absence, and directed that notice be served.
Unlike the original land award, the supplementary award did not contain a term barring a request for further compensation or statutory benefits.
The claimant filed a writ petition challenging the adequacy of the supplementary compensation within six months of the award and before receiving the awarded amount.
The claimant received the supplementary award amount only after filing the writ petition.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was to be given an opportunity to apply to the Land Acquisition Collector for a reference seeking enhanced compensation and other original benefits in respect of the supplementary award. If the application was made within four weeks, the Collector was directed to refer it to the competent court within a month, and that court was directed to decide it expeditiously, preferably within six months.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, a person interested who has not accepted an award may seek a reference to the court. Section 18(2) sets the ordinary time limits for seeking a reference. The Himachal Pradesh proviso added to Section 18 by Himachal Pradesh Act 17 of 1986 permits the Collector, on sufficient cause, to entertain an application after six weeks but within six months. In the circumstances here, the timely writ petition challenging the supplementary award, the direction to serve notice of that award, and receipt of payment only after the writ petition was filed showed that the claimant had not accepted the award. The waiver in the award concerning land did not bar a request concerning the separately awarded structures and trees, where the supplementary award contained no such waiver. No earlier cases were relied upon.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_challenge and supplementary_award_for_nonland_assets and supplementary_award_made_in_absence and no_explicit_waiver_in_supplementary_award and writ_filed_within_six_months and payment_received_after_writ

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_challenge: The proceeding concerns a claimant’s challenge to compensation awarded for acquired property.
predicates.supplementary_award_for_nonland_assets: A supplementary award separately fixes compensation for assets other than the land itself.
predicates.supplementary_award_made_in_absence: The supplementary award is made without the claimant present.
predicates.no_explicit_waiver_in_supplementary_awar: The supplementary award does not state that the claimant gives up the right to seek further compensation or benefits.
predicates.writ_filed_within_six_months: The claimant files a writ challenging the adequacy of the supplementary award within six months of that award.
predicates.payment_received_after_writ: The claimant receives the awarded amount only after filing the writ challenging the award.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition compensation challenge concerns a supplementary award for non-land assets, and the award is made in the claimant’s absence without an express waiver, a timely writ filed before receipt of payment permits the claimant to apply for a reference.
